subject: Nanotechnology
title: Feynman's Bold Vision
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Feynman's Bold Vision.

hook.text: In 1959, Feynman asked why we cannot write the entire Encyclopaedia Britannica on a pin head.

buildup.text: His famous talk 'There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom' imagined engineering at the atomic scale.

discovery.text: He proposed tiny machines building tinier machines, shrinking all the way down to individual atoms.

twist.text: For twenty years nobody acted on his vision — the tools to manipulate atoms did not exist.

climax.text: Today that lecture is considered the founding moment of nanotechnology — a prophecy fulfilled.

punchline.text: Feynman saw the nanoworld before anyone could reach it.

quiz.question: What did Feynman propose in his 1959 lecture?
options: Engineering at the scale of individual atoms
Replacing silicon with graphene in computers
